Technical SEO Checks Before Launching a Website

Review crawlable pages, titles, canonical URLs, internal links and sitemap coverage before introducing your website to search engines.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read

In this guide

Give each useful page a clear purposeCheck what can be discoveredChoose your preferred URLsCreate and inspect the sitemapReview after publishing

Give each useful page a clear purpose

A service page should answer a specific visitor need, with a descriptive title and a meaningful main heading. Avoid creating nearly identical pages just to target spelling variations. A page about API integration should explain the problems it solves, the decisions involved and the next step for someone who needs that service.

Check what can be discovered

Make important destinations available through ordinary links. Open each URL directly rather than only through the menu. Confirm that missing pages return a real not-found response. A site that displays its homepage for every unknown URL makes it harder to distinguish valid content from mistakes.

Choose your preferred URLs

Be consistent about the domain and URL structure. If both a www and a non-www address exist, choose the intended version and configure redirects deliberately. Add canonical tags that point to the public URL you want indexed. Do not accidentally copy preview-domain addresses into the production metadata.

Create and inspect the sitemap

A sitemap lists the public URLs you want search engines to discover. Include real article pages and exclude internal APIs, test pages and private tools. Google explains that a sitemap aids discovery but does not guarantee indexing. Check that every listed URL loads successfully and matches the canonical URL on the page.

Review after publishing

Submit the sitemap in Search Console when you have access, then monitor indexing and search queries. Measure qualified visits and enquiries alongside impressions. Publishing content creates an opportunity to earn visibility; it does not promise a particular ranking. Improve pages based on the questions visitors actually need answered.
